belief: If God doesn’t do a miracle, He doesn’t care.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that if God doesn’t do a miracle He doesn’t care, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Praying desperately for a miracle that did not come. Losing someone you begged God to save. Hearing others’ miracle stories and feeling forgotten. Believing love always shows itself by fixing problems right away. A parent who showed love only by giving what you wanted.
teaches: God’s love is not measured by whether He does what we ask. Jesus loved Mary, Martha, and Lazarus, and yet He waited two days before going to them. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego trusted God whether or not He rescued them from the furnace. God’s ways are higher than ours. He invites you to cast all your anxiety on Him because He cares for you, even when the answer is “no” or “not yet.”
self_statements: If God loved me, He would have fixed this.
God helps other people but not me.
My prayers don’t matter to Him.
Unanswered prayer means God doesn’t care.
I can’t trust a God who says no.
errors: Concluding you know God’s heart from one outcome.
Believing God either does a miracle or doesn’t love you.
Concluding “I feel forgotten, so God must not care.”
Measuring God’s love for you by what He did for others.
questions: Did Jesus love Lazarus’ family even while He waited?
What did the three men in the furnace say they would do if God did not rescue them?
Are God’s ways always my ways?
What evidence of God’s care can I see apart from this miracle?
What does 1 Peter 5:7 say about God’s care for me?
Can I trust God’s love even when I don’t understand His answer?
Has God ever said no to me before and later I saw why?
truth: God cares for me even when He does not do the miracle I ask for. His love is not measured by whether He gives me what I want. Jesus loved Lazarus’ family even while He waited. God’s ways are higher than mine. I can cast all my anxiety on Him because He cares for me.
hw_questions: Did Jesus love Lazarus’ family while He waited?
What did the men in the furnace say?
Are God’s ways always my ways?
What other evidence of God’s care can I see?
What does 1 Peter 5:7 say about me?
Has God said no before for my good?
hw_truths: God cares for me even when He says no.
God’s love is not measured by miracles.
God’s ways are higher than my ways.
I can cast all my anxiety on Him because He cares.
God is the strength of my heart.
God works all things together for my good.
log: Each day, write one way I saw God’s care for me that was not a miracle.
name_example: Sarah can cast all her anxiety on Him, because He cares for her.
actions: and write how Jesus showed love both before and after the miracle.
and write what the three men believed about God whether or not He rescued them.
Tell God honestly how disappointed you are,
then name one way He has cared for you.
Share your unanswered prayer with a trusted believer
and ask them to pray with you.
prayer: Father, I am disappointed that You did not do what I asked. Help me reject the lie that You don’t care because You didn’t do a miracle. Thank You that Your ways are higher than mine and that You care for me. Help me trust Your love even when I don’t understand. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
songs: Jesus understands suffering and invites people to bring their burdens to Him.
Weariness can be expressed honestly while asking God for restoration.
God’s faithful presence challenges the expectation of rejection and abandonment.
What a Friend We Have in Jesus
This classic hymn invites direct, honest prayer with the Savior who carries our burdens.
